Hi Olga,

Jacob,

Appreciate the clarity — we can deliver a single consolidated package. Summary of deliverables we will attach:
- VM runbook (PDF): SAST/DAST process, tooling, triage/playbook, evidence mapping.
- SAST/DAST cadence table (XLSX): scan schedules, scan types, false-positive workflow, ownership.
- Pen-test executive summary (PDF): scope, high/medium findings summary, mitigation status and ETA.
- SBOM provenance CSV: module origin, checksum, license, last-scanned date and transitive mapping.

Quick answers to your explicit asks:
- SAST/DAST tooling: we run static analysis with CodeScan Pro and dynamic scans with DynaProbe; both are automated in CI and scheduled weekly for prod branches.
- Tracking: findings flow into Jira with a Redwood vulnerability label and severity tag; remediation SLA timers are attached to each ticket.
- Remediation SLAs: we map by CVSS-equivalent severity and by environment (see table attached). For production-critical P1s we target 72 hours to mitigation and 7 days to verified fix; P2s are 14 days; P3s 30 days.

We will attach the first-draft package in this thread by EOD. Neha will include the technical runbook notes and the exact Jira query filters for evidence exports. Karthik will add the pen-test brief.

Jacob / Olga,

Attaching the technical supplements per Olga's note. Highlights here to call out before you dive into the attachments:

- SAST cadence and outputs:
  - Pre-merge checks run on every PR (fast mode).
  - Nightly full-scan for prod branches (CodeScan Pro full-analysis).
  - Weekly DAST on staging mirrors using DynaProbe; critical endpoints fuzzed monthly.
  - False positives: triage label + reproducibility steps required; false positives are closed only after QA sign-off.

- Ticketing & evidence export:
  - Vulnerability tickets created in Jira using project INFSEC, vulnerability-type field filled from scanner signatures.
  - Evidence export: CSV with scanner id, CWE, file:line, git-commit, SCA-id, and suggested remediation link. We included the Jira filter: project = INFSEC AND "Vendor" = Redwood AND created >= -90d for audit pulls.

- Patch / remediation SLA mapping (attached spreadsheet):
  - Prod P1 (remote code exec / active exploit): 72h mitigation window, hotfix or mitigation deployed; targeted verified fix within 7 days.
  - Prod P2 (privilege escalation / high-impact data exposure): 14 days to fix.
  - Prod P3 (low-risk / informational): 30 days backloged in sprint cadence.
  - Non-prod SLAs are relaxed by factor of 2 (e.g., P1 7 days for non-prod).

- SBOM provenance & transitive alert handling:
  - SBOM is generated from build artifacts at release, stored in an immutable bucket; each SBOM row includes package checksum and source registry.
  - We run weekly SCA (software composition analysis) that flags transitive vulnerabilities; triage follows same Jira workflow.
  - For transitive criticals, we evaluate upstream patch availability and apply dependency bump or mitigation; we maintain a short-lived fork if upstream patching is not immediate.

I've included the SAST/DAST cadence spreadsheet and a small SBOM export for the web-service component. Let me know if you want the full org-wide SBOM; that is a larger CSV and we can provide via secure transfer.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor

Jacob — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the pen-test executive summary (redacted for customer-facing release) and a short mitigation status table. Executive notes:

- Scope: external network and application-layer assessments covering our public inference endpoints and internal admin consoles.
- Findings: 2 high (both remediated), 5 medium (3 remediated, 2 scheduled), 8 low. Highs were related to a third-party dependency which we patched and rolled out within 48 hours; full verification completed in 6 days.
- Residual risk: low (monitoring enabled) — post-mitigation verification done and evidence attached in the runbook.

Marcus included a short note on SBOM provenance: every release SBOM is signed and checksummed; we retain SBOM snapshots per release tag for audit. We can provide a signed SBOM bundle via an S3 presigned link if you prefer that over a raw CSV.

If that meets your needs, Olga / I can provide a single zipped package and a brief cover letter for your procurement team.

Thanks,
